newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa to clean up waste, eco-impact policy.
newsitem.headline: South Africa to clean up waste, eco-impact policy.

text.p: South Africa is to make impact assessments compulsory for new projects that might affect the enviroment, Environment Minister Pallo Jordan said on Tuesday.
He said in a speech to parliament that new "holistic" guidelines were also being formulated on waste management.

Jordan said economic growth was the first imperative of South African government policy, but added that the "unbridled and unregulated pursuit of private profit" of the past would no longer be allowed.
"We have resolved to embark on a different path... In the past South Africa did not bother much about the environmental impact of economic activity," he said.

"While it is not yet routine to undertake environmental impact assessments, our new national evnironmental policy, soon to be unveiled as a white paper, will make these compulsory in future," Jordan said.
He said there was no intention to constrain growth, but development had to be "more equitable, less polluting, more efficient in the use of energy and natural resources".
Jordan said Denmark had provided 9.5 million rand and a team of experts, who would arrive in August, to help develop a waste management strategy.
"There is a need to move away from end-of-pipe solutions for waste and pollution, to concepts like cleaner production, clean technology, waste minimisation and pollution prevention," he said.
